title: Microsoft 365 Copilot: MCP-based agents for US Government clouds
summary: The briefing accurately reports the roadmap launch while preserving Microsoft's conflicting government-cloud support statements. The blocking path, preview API restrictions, general agent entitlements and GCC tool-access capability are supported by the current documentation.

claims.claim: The item concerns MCP-based agent enablement in Microsoft 365 Copilot for US Government clouds.
claims.quote: Microsoft Copilot (Microsoft 365): MCP-Based Agent Enablement for U.S. Government Clouds

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; Open questions; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Separate MCP-specific government licensing terms are not published in the researched sources.
claims.quote: Searched: Microsoft 365 Copilot MCP agents government licensing pricing GCC GCCH DoD; "MCP" "government" licensing. Read prerequisites, Copilot service description, license-options excerpts and MCP walkthrough; found general entitlements but no separate terms for this enablement.

claims.claim: Learn does not specifically describe roadmap item 564607's government-cloud MCP enablement.
claims.quote: Searched: Microsoft 365 Copilot MCP government GCC GCC High DoD default rollout licensing MCP servers. Opened MCP walkthrough, plugin overview, declarative-agent overview, prerequisites and known issues; these give general MCP guidance and cloud restrictions, not this item's implementation.

claims.claim: The walkthrough's plugin manifest connects a declarative agent to a remote MCP server.
claims.quote: This walkthrough creates a declarative agent with an MCP plugin. The plugin manifest connects the agent to a remote MCP server

claims.claim: The manifest does not package or host the running MCP server.
claims.quote: The plugin manifest connects the agent to a remote MCP server; it doesn't package or host the running server.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Change & support
claims.claim: MCP plugins used as declarative-agent actions resolve tools dynamically from the server at runtime by default.
claims.quote: For plugins based on an MCP server, Copilot resolves the plugin's tools dynamically at runtime by default, directly from the MCP server.

claims.claim: A developer can instead pin a fixed tool set in the plugin manifest.
claims.quote: When building the agent, a developer can optionally pin a fixed set of tools in the plugin manifest instead.

claims.claim: The Microsoft Copilot service description lists declarative agents as not currently available in DoD.
claims.quote:
| Feature | Commercial/Worldwide | GCC | GCCH | DoD |
| Declarative agents | Yes | Yes | Yes⁸ | Not currently available |

claims.claim: That service description limits GCC High to declarative agents made with Agent Builder or published through admin controls.
claims.quote: GCC-High currently only supports declarative agents created using Agent Builder and those published via admin controls.

claims.claim: The declarative-agent overview instead states that DoD supports only pro-code agents built with Microsoft 365 Agents Toolkit.
claims.quote: Department of Defense (DoD): Limited support - only pro-code agents built with Microsoft 365 Agents Toolkit are supported. Agent Builder isn't available for declarative agents in DoD.

claims.claim: The declarative-agent overview supports Toolkit-built pro-code agents in GCCH.
claims.quote: Government Community Cloud High (GCCH): Pro-code agents built with Microsoft 365 Agents Toolkit are supported.

claims.claim: The declarative-agent overview also says Agent Builder is available in GCCH.
claims.quote: Agent Builder is also now available in GCCH.

claims.quote: Searched: Microsoft 365 Copilot MCP server government data boundary GCC GCC High DoD tools access controls; "MCP" "government" boundary. Read plugin overview, data-privacy-security and gov-overview excerpts; no item-specific external-server boundary assurance was found.

claims.quote: Agents grounded in shared tenant work data aren't currently available in Microsoft 365 Government Community Cloud (GCC), Government Community Cloud High (GCCH), or Department of Defense (DoD) environments.

claims.claim: The walkthrough uses an OAuth registration to obtain a token on behalf of the signed-in user on each MCP server call.
claims.quote: Copilot then uses the registration to obtain an access token on behalf of the signed-in user each time the agent calls the MCP server.

claims.claim: A server without authentication can use the None authentication type during development.
claims.quote: If your MCP server is still in development and doesn't implement authentication, select None as the authentication type.

claims.claim: Learn instructs developers to add authentication before production deployment.
claims.quote: Add authentication before you deploy to production.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Security & identity
claims.claim: MCP plugins are custom actions, so the documented authenticated-custom-action Government restriction encompasses authenticated MCP actions.
claims.quote: MCP and API plugins are custom actions that enable declarative agents in Microsoft 365 Copilot to interact with Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers or REST APIs

claims.where: Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; rationale: risk
claims.claim: MCP and API plugins can, when supported, create, update and delete connected-system data through natural-language prompts.
claims.quote: users can ask a declarative agent to query an MCP server or REST API for information and, when supported, create, update, and delete data and objects through natural language prompts.

claims.claim: Dynamic discovery can change the available tool set without repackaging or republishing the agent.
claims.quote: Dynamic tool discovery means you get the latest tools the MCP server exposes without waiting for the agent to be repackaged and republished.

claims.claim: Microsoft has not specified rollout mechanics for this item in the researched documentation.
claims.quote: Searched: Microsoft 365 Copilot MCP based agents government GCC GCCH DoD default enable rollout admin switch. Read roadmap record, MCP walkthrough, prerequisites, known issues and release-notes excerpts; no rollout mechanism for this item was found.

claims.claim: Agents published by the organisation go through administrator approval before becoming available to its members.
claims.quote: Before you make these agents available to members of your organization, these agents go through an admin approval to ensure compliance and readiness.

claims.claim: Administrators can review agents at Microsoft 365 admin center > Agents > All agents.
claims.quote:
Select Agents > All agents.
In the All agents page, select an agent from the list of agents.

claims.claim: The organisation-wide block route is Microsoft 365 admin center > Agents > All agents > agent > Block > Block agent > Save.
claims.quote: Select Agents > All agents. ... select an agent from the list of agents. ... select Block or Unblock. ... select either Block agent or Unblock agent, and then select Save.

claims.claim: POST https://graph.microsoft.com/beta/copilot/admin/catalog/packages/{id}/block blocks the selected Copilot package.
claims.quote:
Block a Copilot package to prevent its usage.
POST https://graph.microsoft.com/beta/copilot/admin/catalog/packages/{id}/block
Don't supply a request body for this method.

claims.claim: The general agent block control restricts agent use across the whole organisation using the same controls as other apps.
claims.quote: Block or unblock agents for the entire organization by using the same controls that work for any other app in the Microsoft 365 admin center.

claims.claim: Blocking the selected agent need not block a shared MCP server.
claims.quote: These actions apply to the selected agent. If the agent is included in a plugin, don't assume the action also applies to the whole plugin package, its skills, shared MCP servers, or connections.

claims.claim: Agent blocking does not necessarily revoke connected-service permissions or credentials.
claims.quote: Agent approval or blocking doesn't necessarily grant or revoke connected-service permissions or credentials.

claims.claim: The package-block API is a preview Microsoft Graph beta operation.
claims.quote: | Block (preview) | POST /copilot/admin/catalog/packages/{id}/block | Block a package to prevent its usage. |

claims.claim: MCP tool invocation is subject to the server's authentication requirements.
